description: Excel-style cell visualisations in the Svelte 5 data grid written as user-land cell snippets: a red to yellow to green colour scale, in-cell data bars proportional to the value, a traffic-light icon set by threshold and a heat-map tint across a row. Each renderer reads its column's min and max from the displayed rows and paints accordingly, and a side panel toggles every formatter on and off to compare.

faq.question: How does a cell know the column's range?
faq.answer: A $derived computes min and max per column from the current rows once; each cell snippet reads them and maps its value to a colour or a bar width.

faq.question: Is there a built-in way to do this?
faq.answer: Yes. The conditionalFormats prop does colour scales, data bars, icon sets and predicate rules declaratively; this demo shows the same effects hand-built so you can see what the engine saves you.

faq.question: Can I mix formatters on one column?
faq.answer: Yes. A snippet can paint a background tint and an icon at once; the toggles in the side panel show each layer independently.
